entries.title: Rejected from YC last night... got anchor client this morning
entries.author: chinup
entries.current_title: Rejected from YC last night... got anchor client this morning
entries.excerpt: Like others, we were down about our YC rejection last night. This morning, we got a commitment from an anchor client (we target small/medium businesses). It took 15 minutes to convince the owner of this multi-million dollar business to say: "I love it." We built a demo for our customers and decided to send it to YC as well. entries.title: YC got a record number of applications this cycle
entries.author: pg
entries.current_title: YC got a record number of applications this cycle
entries.excerpt: One bit of good news about the economy: would-be startup founders don't seem to have been deterred by it, yet at least. YC got more applications this time than ever, and by a large margin: 10%. The number usually goes up, but rarely so sharply. It wasn't due to the essay I just wrote about starting a startup in a bad economy. We were already on track for a record before that. entries.title: Ask HN: Is clojure (lisp in JVM) next big thing?
entries.author: btw0
entries.current_title: Ask HN: Is clojure (lisp in JVM) next big thing?
entries.excerpt: There seems to be a lot of people even some intelligent ones who are lately talking about and exploring clojure, a new lisp dialect run in JVM. It looks really promising, but a lot of people especially lisp programmers have an inherent hatred in java. How is that? what do you think about this ``lisp in JVM''? Is the clojure the future of lisp?
